ponytail.what: Write as little code as possible
ponytail.how:
Passive: once enabled, it applies on its own to every coding answer. Active: the review and audit commands are launched by hand.
Levels, chosen in its band above the prompt or with /ponytail:ponytail <level>:
• off: turned off, Claude works normally.
• lite: builds what is asked as is, and points out a simpler version in one line if there is one.
• full (default): the smallest change that fully solves the problem, with no option, abstraction or dependency nobody asked for.
• ultra: like full, and also questions the request itself before building.
At every level, nothing that was asked for is skipped, nor security, nor what protects data.
ponytail.why: Avoid unneeded code, useless abstractions and dependencies added for a few lines.
ponytail.when: Whenever you write, fix or refactor code.
ponytail.hint: You are about to touch code: ponytail keeps the change minimal.

agent-skills.what: Engineering method: specify, plan, test, review, ship
agent-skills.how: Passive: Claude loads the right skill for the task on its own (TDD, debugging, security…). Active: the /agent-skills:… commands are launched by hand.
agent-skills.why: Follow a proven process instead of coding straight away.
agent-skills.when: New feature, bug to trace, review before merge, release, security, performance.
agent-skills.hint: A method task: spec, plan, test or review depending on the stage.

graphify.what: Turn a code folder into a knowledge graph
graphify.how: You run /graphify to build the graph (in graphify-out/). Then a hook points Claude to the graph on its own.
graphify.why: Understand an unknown or large project: what calls what, which files are linked.
graphify.when: Architecture question, project to explore or forgotten.
graphify.hint: A question about the project's structure: /graphify . then /graphify query.

anthropic-skills.what: Anthropic skills: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, browser, research
anthropic-skills.how: Passive: Claude loads the right skill on its own when the task involves an office file or the browser. Active: some are launched by hand, like deep research or skill creation.
anthropic-skills.why: Read and produce office files correctly, drive the browser, create your own skills.
anthropic-skills.when: You handle a .pdf, .docx, .xlsx or .pptx, want documented research, or want to create a skill.
anthropic-skills.hint: Office file, browser or research: an Anthropic skill handles it.

rea.what: Reverse engineering: analyze a program without its source code
rea.how: Passive: Claude uses the REA tools on its own when you ask it to analyze an .exe, a .dll, an Electron, .NET or Android app. Active: you point it to the file to analyze. On Windows, Ghidra only does read-only analysis of Windows programs (.exe, .dll).
rea.why: Understand what existing software does, check a suspicious file, recover how an old program works.
rea.when: You have an executable, a library or an app whose source code you don't have.
ex: Decompile the main function of this .exe
What does this Electron app do?
rea.hint: Analyzing a program without source code: REA and Ghidra.

Unity CLI.what: Drive the Unity editor from the command line
Unity CLI.how: A program installed on the computer (not a plugin). The Unity plugin's skills use it to drive the open editor: scenes, assets, C#, playing the game, screenshots, compiling. Important: each Unity project must be created with the Unity Pipeline package, otherwise the CLI cannot take over the editor.
Unity CLI.why: Let Claude act in Unity without the mouse.
Unity CLI.when: Create a project, install an editor or a package, compile, test, edit a scene.
ex: Create a new Unity 2D project with the Unity Pipeline package
Unity CLI.hint: Working in Unity: the Unity CLI and the Unity plugin can act in the editor.

llm-council.what: Have five AI advisors debate a decision
llm-council.how: You launch it with a trigger phrase. Claude can also suggest it on its own for a real choice. Eleven model calls per session; writes an HTML report and a transcript in the folder.
llm-council.why: Test an important choice against the complacency of a single answer.
llm-council.when: A real decision with stakes and several options, not a factual question.
ex: council this: plain PHP or a framework for this project?
debate this: SQL or JSON files
